title: chenopodium ambrosioides var. genuinum
intro: Chenopodium ambrosioides var. genuinum, commonly known as Mexican tea or epazote, is a plant species native to the Americas, belonging to the family Amaranthaceae. Mexican tea has been used for centuries in traditional medicine, particularly in Mexican and Central American folk medicine, for its purported health benefits, including the treatment of digestive issues, nausea, and respiratory problems. The plant's therapeutic actions include its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antispasmodic properties, which contribute to its use in relieving symptoms of various conditions. The bioactive constituents of Mexican tea include alkaloids, flavonoids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and health benefits.
